title: Can You See Me Now?

pre.en: What could Chen see during the first video call?
pre.zh: 第一次视频通话时，Chen 看到了什么？

intro: 一个小故事：Chen 给成都的爸妈买了平板电脑，花了一个下午替他们设置好，还写了一页中文说明。读的时候留意，Chen 做的每件事都有个目的：to do、in order to、so as not to 这几种说法，把「为了什么」「免得什么」说得清清楚楚。最后是第一次视频通话。

sentences.en: Chen's parents in Chengdu have never really been into technology.
sentences.zh: 小陈在成都的爸妈，对科技产品一直不怎么感冒。

sentences.en: His dad has struggled with his smartphone for years, and his mum only uses hers to check the weather.
sentences.zh: 他爸爸跟智能手机较劲了好几年，他妈妈的手机只拿来看天气。

sentences.en: So in October, Chen splashed out £560 on two tablets, one for himself and one for them.
sentences.zh: 所以十月份，小陈一咬牙花了 560 英镑买了两台平板，一台自己用，一台给爸妈。

sentences.en: The plan was to see each other every Sunday, not just hear each other.
sentences.zh: 他的打算是：每个星期天，一家人不光能听见声音，还能见上面。

sentences.en: He spent the whole of Saturday afternoon setting up the one for his parents.
sentences.zh: 星期六整个下午，他都在给爸妈那台做设置。

sentences.en: In order to make it as simple as possible, he made all the icons bigger.
sentences.zh: 为了让它用起来越简单越好，他把所有图标都调大了。

sentences.en: Then he put one big green button on the screen to make a video call.
sentences.zh: 然后在屏幕上放了一个大大的绿色按钮，专门用来打视频电话。

sentences.en: He even signed in to every app for them, so as not to get calls about lost passwords.
sentences.zh: 他还替爸妈把每个 App 都登录好了，免得以后老接到「密码找不到了」的电话。

sentences.en: He was so passionate about the project that he forgot to eat lunch.
sentences.zh: 他干得太投入，连午饭都忘了吃。

sentences.en: Tom offered to help out.
sentences.zh: Tom 主动说要来搭把手。

sentences.en: As it turned out, Tom's only job was to say "Wow" every time Chen showed him a screen.
sentences.zh: 结果 Tom 唯一的活儿，就是小陈每给他看一个界面，他就说一声「哇」。

sentences.en: Next, Chen wrote a one-page guide in Chinese, in order not to confuse his dad.
sentences.zh: 接着，小陈用中文写了一页说明，免得把爸爸弄糊涂。

sentences.en: It had three steps: switch it on, press the green button, wait.
sentences.zh: 一共三步：开机，按绿色按钮，等着。

sentences.en: At the bottom, he added, "If you get lost, just put your hand up and wait."
sentences.zh: 最下面他又加了一句：「要是不知道怎么弄了，举个手，等着就行。」

sentences.en: He wanted to be patient with his dad.
sentences.zh: 他想对爸爸耐心一点。

sentences.en: When Chen was nine, he'd broken the family computer, and his dad hadn't even told him off.
sentences.zh: 小陈九岁那年把家里的电脑弄坏了，爸爸连一句都没骂他。

sentences.en: "They're going to love it," Tom said.
sentences.zh: 「他们肯定会喜欢的。」Tom 说。

sentences.en: Ten days later, the parcel arrived in Chengdu.
sentences.zh: 十天后，包裹到了成都。

sentences.en: On Sunday at one o'clock — nine in the evening there — Chen sat at his desk and waited.
sentences.zh: 星期天下午一点——成都那边是晚上九点——小陈坐在书桌前等着。

sentences.en: To his surprise, his dad had got everything up and running in under a minute.
sentences.zh: 没想到，爸爸不到一分钟就把一切都弄好了。

sentences.en: It would take them weeks to get a feel for it, but Dad was already pressing buttons that weren't in the guide.
sentences.zh: 他们得花好几个星期才能摸到门道，可爸爸已经在按说明上没写的按钮了。

sentences.en: The call connected, and his mum's voice filled the room.
sentences.zh: 电话一接通，屋里一下子全是妈妈的声音。

sentences.en: "We can see you perfectly!" she shouted.
sentences.zh: 「我们看你看得清清楚楚！」她大声说。

sentences.en: "Can you see us?"
sentences.zh: 「你看得见我们吗？」

sentences.en: Chen looked closely.
sentences.zh: 小陈凑近看了看。

sentences.en: "Well, I can see your ceiling," he said.
sentences.zh: 「嗯，我看得见你们家天花板，」他说。

sentences.en: "It needs painting."
sentences.zh: 「该刷漆了。」

cards.note: to be very interested in an activity or subject and enjoy it
重音在第二个音节 /tekˈnɒlədʒi/；形容词 technical。
to find something very difficult to do, use or deal with
cards.tip: 后面接名词或 doing：struggle with maths / struggle with getting up early；想努力做到某事用 struggle to do。
cards.example: I always struggle with the self-service machines at the supermarket.

cards.note: to spend a lot of money on something, usually something you do not really need
原意是「药片」，看上下文分辨。
to get a machine or a piece of equipment ready so that it can be used
cards.tip: 宾语是代词时放中间：set it up；也可以说「创办」：set up a company。过去式、过去分词都是 set。
cards.example: It took me an hour to set up the new printer.

cards.note: 读 /ˈaɪkɒn/，开头是 /aɪ/。
to call someone using a phone or computer so that you can see each other while you talk
cards.tip: 动词用 make，不用 do 或 play；打给谁用 to sb 或直接说 video-call sb。
cards.example: We make a video call to my grandma every Friday evening.

cards.note: to type your name and password so that you can use a website or an app
cards.tip: 登录到哪里用 sign in to；退出是 sign out。也常说 log in / log out。
cards.example: You need to sign in before you can leave a review.

cards.note: 改密码是 change your password；忘了密码是 forget your password。
to have very strong feelings of love or interest for something
to help someone, especially when they are busy
形容词 confused（人觉得糊涂）、confusing（事情让人糊涂）。
to make a machine, a light or a piece of equipment start working by pressing a button
cards.tip: 英式常用 switch on / off，美式多说 turn on / off；宾语是代词时放中间：switch it on。
cards.example: Can you switch on the heating? It's freezing in here.

cards.note: to raise your arm in a class or meeting because you want to answer or ask something
cards.tip: your 要跟着人称变：put my hand up、put their hands up；也可以说 raise your hand。
cards.example: Put your hand up if you need more paper.

cards.note: to speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong
cards.tip: 为什么挨训用 for + doing；「挨训」常说 get told off。
cards.example: The driver told us off for eating on the bus.

cards.note: 英式说 parcel，美式多说 package；寄包裹是 send / post a parcel。

cards.zh: 让（系统、设备）运转起来；弄好能用
cards.note: to make a machine, a system or a business start working properly
cards.tip: 也可以只说 be up and running（已经能用了）；常说的是系统、网站、项目这类东西。
cards.example: The new website should be up and running by Friday.

cards.zh: 摸到……的门道；找到……的感觉
cards.note: to start to understand how to do something or how something works
cards.tip: feel 在这里是名词，前面要有 a；已经有感觉了说 have a feel for sth。
cards.example: Drive slowly at first until you get a feel for the car.

cards.note: 连 Wi-Fi 是 connect to the Wi-Fi；名词 connection。
